paras: The killing of Jeff Davis's wife at Lake City was the fatal stabbing of a Black woman by three white men near Lake City, Williamsburg County, South Carolina, reported in November 1888. She was killed while trying to protect her son, whom the men were beating, and the dispatch reporting the killing said the attackers remained at large with no effort made to arrest them.

According to a dispatch from Columbia dated November 22, Jeff Davis and his wife, both described as "colored," were returning from church in Lake City when they met Merritt Ferrett, Belle Gray and Alex Smiley, all white. The dispatch said the three men were "under the influence of whiskey" and held a grudge against the Davises' son.

The men began beating the son and drew knives on him. To protect him, his mother picked up a piece of fence rail and started toward the attackers. The men then turned on her and stabbed her in the breast and heart eight or ten times, killing her instantly. The dispatch does not give the date of the killing or the names of the woman and her son.

At the time of the report the three men were at large, and the correspondent wrote that no efforts were being made to bring them to justice. Black residents of the neighborhood were described as "wild with excitement," and the dispatch warned that "serious results may follow" unless something was done. No report of an arrest, inquest or trial appears in the coverage.

The only report found ran in the New York Sun on November 23, 1888, as a short item headed "Brutal Murder of a Colored Woman." The item named the white attackers, called them "murderers," and pointed to the absence of any effort to prosecute them, while presenting the Black community's reaction as a possible source of trouble. No South Carolina paper's version and no Black-press coverage was found.

bases: Three white men beat a Black man and stabbed his mother to death when she came to his defense, acting on a grudge rather than as an organized band or in response to an accusation (A1).

accounts.label: Columbia dispatch
accounts.gist: Three drunken white men with a grudge against Davis's son beat him and drew knives; when his mother came at them with a fence rail they stabbed her to death, and they remained at large with no effort made to arrest them.

framing.detail: The Sun headlined it 'Brutal Murder of a Colored Woman', called the attackers 'murderers', and noted that no efforts were being made to bring them to justice.
